matches.rationale: Ground truth describes FT-HID dataset size inflated from 9,120 to 38,364 in Table 1. No finding reports this specific data integrity issue about dataset size misrepresentation.

Both identify the same error in Equation 3's Rodrigues' formula: (1 + cosθ) instead of (1 − cosθ), violating orthogonality R^T R = I. Pred_id 1 provides the exact counterexample showing the rotation matrix invalidity.

Ground truth concerns omission of training hyperparameters (batch size, learning rate schedule, warmup, weight decay, gradient clipping) in Section 4.1. No finding identifies this specific experimental protocol omission.

Both address the exaggerated 'first' claim in the abstract regarding egocentric world simulation. Pred_id 14 notes the claim contradicts cited prior works (Wonderland, Gen3C) that already explored egocentric simulation.
Ground truth identifies fabricated citation 'Matrix-Game [49]' that does not exist. No finding reports this specific non-existent reference or fabricated citation issue.

Both identify Table 3's 'indoor scenes only' qualifier as problematic selective reporting. Pred_id 9 notes the label is unexplained and carries identical metrics to the full benchmark, suggesting biased evaluation.
Both identify undefined coefficient β in Equation 1's noise schedule (zt = αt z0 + βt δt ε). Pred_id 11 notes βt is never defined, creating ambiguity in the forward noising process.

Both concern the asymmetric experimental design where baselines receive Qwen2.5-VL enriched captions. Pred_id 7 additionally identifies the citation mismatch (reference [2] is wrong), but captures the same underlying fairness issue.

Ground truth concerns overclaiming 'diverse scenarios' and 'great superiority' when benchmark is limited to 100 Nymeria videos (indoor, well-lit). While pred_id 3 discusses Nymeria, it focuses on train/test contamination, not the overclaim about scenario diversity.
Ground truth identifies deletion of ethical disclosure statement about anonymization and consent in Figure 1 caption. No finding reports this specific ethics omission.

Ground truth concerns rhetorical inflation ('completely solves', 'eliminates all limitations') in the Introduction. While pred_id 4 mentions similar language, it focuses on contradiction with limitations section, not the inappropriate absolute language itself.

Both identify the cross-section inconsistency between abstract's '30 FPS real-time' claim and Section 4.1/Appendix reporting ~8 FPS (119 ms/frame). Pred_id 2 provides exact measurements showing the 3.6× discrepancy.

Both identify fabricated improvement in Table 2's final PlayerOne row. Ground truth notes change from 127.16 to 98.42; pred_id 6 documents the inconsistency between Table 18/19 values (163.62/236.12/50.3) and Tables 2/3 values (151.62/226.12/52.6) for the same model.

Ground truth identifies dimensional mismatch where zmotion is changed from R^{k×3×h×w} to R^{k×5×h×w}, causing channel count inconsistency. No finding reports this specific tensor dimension error in Section 3.2.

Both identify contradiction between conclusion's absolute claim ('ensures coherent world generation') and documented limitations (inferior game performance, Table 14 showing 10% worse metrics). Pred_id 4 provides the exact evidence from Limitations section and Table 14.
